title: Customer clarity brief and low-touch probe index — 2027-11-21
content:
Purpose
---
Short working brief to translate recent field signal into a tiny, actionable index of low-effort probes and a one-page clarity summary for PMs and EngSRE. This is intentionally lightweight — the goal is to validate which microfixes reduce friction fastest and which themes need scoped projects.

Context and sources
---
Inputs in the last 6 weeks: developer session recordings (3), support convo threads (12), post-demo feedback from three pilot customers, two SRE incident reviews, and survey replies from 42 customers (NPS follow-up). I pulled out representative quotes below and clustered by observable pain. Tickets and PRs referenced in linked_artifacts.

Top themes (quick read)
---
1) Observability blind spots: customers want token-level cost breakdowns that map to routes/models (not just aggregated invoices). This shows up as 'we can't blame the model when cost spikes' and 'need per-route token SLOs for budgeting'.
2) Latency tail cases: most requests are fast, but a small percentage (0.5–1%) hit large latency spikes tied to long contexts and KV cache misses.
3) Routing/fallback clarity: when Dedicated capacity is saturated, apps observed opaque fallbacks to smaller models without clear logs/alerts.
4) Config-as-code discoverability: multiple teams requested simpler ways to export route configs and rollout policies as YAML to put into infra repos.
5) Small dev ergonomics: function calling examples and streaming mismatch in SDKs; error surface is confusing in intermittent network conditions.

Representative customer snippets
---
- "Our billing jumped 3x after onboarding beta users. We have no per-route token view to debug who caused it." — mid-market SaaS exec
- "A handful of requests take >2s and ruin SLAs for interactive features. We saw those only after we instrumented extra logging." — platform engineer
- "During a Dedicated maintenance window our app silently used the hosted model and returned hallucinated outputs — no alert, no fallback log." — security-sensitive enterprise

Quick impact/effort framing (for prioritization)
---
- Token-level route breakdown (impact: high, effort: medium) — solves immediate billing/debugging friction and reduces CS tickets.
- KV cache telemetry (impact: medium-high, effort: low) — expose cache hit/miss per-route and per-model, plus a small dashboard.
- Fallback transparency (impact: high, effort: medium) — surface events when model routing falls back (emails + dashboard marker).
- Export route configs (impact: medium, effort: low) — CLI command that dumps route+rollout YAML.
- SDK streaming edge-case doc + small patch (impact: low-medium, effort: low) — doc + tests reproducing common network glitch patterns.

Proposed low-touch probes (fast experiments we can run in 1–3 sprints)
---
1) Route token lens (MVP) — add a per-route token count breakdown to the Console usage page and wire an exported CSV. Backend change: emit route tag with token usage; UI: show top-10 routes. Scope: 2 sprints (backend + tiny UI). Rollout: opt-in per-customer.
2) KV miss alert rule — push a default alert when KV miss rate > 15% for a route over a 5m window. Prototype: create alert recipe in Console, document remediation (increase cache size or warm prefixes). Scope: 1 sprint.
3) Fallback audit log + webhook — when a request is routed to a non-preferred model (fallback), emit an audit event and optional webhook to customers. Prototype using existing event bus; add sample webhook consumer. Scope: 1–2 sprints.
4) Lightweight route-config CLI — leverage existing control-plane APIs to add `redwood export-route --route <id> --format yaml`. Provide examples for CI/CD integration. Scope: 1 sprint.
5) SDK streaming checklist + compatibility test — short doc and test harness that maintainers can run; add to CI. Scope: <1 sprint.

Success metrics for each probe (so we can measure quickly)
---
- Route token lens: % reduction in billing-related CS tickets within 30 days; adoption rate (how many customers opt-in); time-to-resolution (median).
- KV miss alert: % reduction in latency tail incidents attributed to cold cache; # of alerts triggered vs resolved.
- Fallback audit: # of incidents where fallback detected and customer notified before they file a support ticket; reduction in 'silent fallback' complaints.
- CLI export: # of downloads and number of teams referencing it in repos (tracked by linked artifacts or customer mentions).
- SDK checklist: reduced replay of streaming bug reports; green CI runs across maintained SDK matrix.

Open questions & risks
---
- Privacy/Billing alignment: exposing fine-grained token data could reveal internal usage patterns that enterprise customers may consider sensitive. Need legal/finance input on export limits.
- Noise vs signal for alerts: default thresholds might generate chatter; start opt-in and tune using canary customers.
- Event volume for fallback audit: ensure audit events are aggregated, not creating telemetry cost for high-QPS customers.

Suggested immediate next actions (this week)
---
1) PM + EngSRE alignment meeting (30m) to pick top 2 probes to ship as opt-in. Proposed attendees: Priya, Evan, Marta, Alex (runtime), Sam (console).
2) Create three Jira tickets for the chosen probes with clear acceptance criteria and the success metrics above.
3) Identify 3 pilot customers (1 startup, 1 mid-market, 1 enterprise) willing to opt into early telemetry.
4) Quick legal check re: token export policies.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
---
- This doc intentionally keeps scope small. If we try to 'solve observability' as a whole we'll never ship. Low-touch probes are meant to gain evidence and reduce customer pain quickly.
- Feedback requested: which two probes should be first-cut opt-in? Any objections on the linked artifact choices?

Appendix: micro-implementation sketches (very short)
---
- Route token lens: add "route_id" to metrics envelope from serving runtime; dimension in usage aggregation job; surface in Console as table + CSV.
- KV miss alert: runtime emits cache_hit=false metric tagged with route_id; alert query checks rate over time.
- Fallback audit: when router chooses model != preferred, emit event with request_id, route_id, chosen_model, reason; webhook payload sample in linked_artifacts PR.

End of brief
